finding: The one-shot serial reconstruction proof rejects a valid transient BUSY detach response while frontend access remains admitted.

negative_control.result: First replay failed on target; planned remaining two attempts were not run. QEMU was stopped only after the explicit failure, and Make returned exit 2.
negative_control.interpretation: 3200 + pass 0 * 100 + SERIAL_VIRT_ERR_BUSY (3). Reply opcode, length and version were validated first; rebind, enqueue and queue-consumption checks had already passed.

correction.behavior: Retry only well-formed BUSY responses, at most 64 attempts with Yield between attempts. Require OK before capability revocation. Malformed replies, other errors and exhaustion still fail.
correction.host_evidence: Existing tests/platform/test_serial_virt_service.c admits frontend access, observes BUSY without retirement, ends access while preserving CLOSED, rejects late I/O and then requires successful detach. Host, firmware link and full Spark gates at the correction are retained in x86-virtio-retirement.json.

verification.result: One current-revision Intel pass before negative control, then three consecutive corrected-revision runs after it; all terminal exit 0.
verification.managed_regression: The corrected code is also present in runtime 3ea3554, whose host/Spark gates, two pinned Debian SSH/input/destroy cycles and native GUI two-boot cycles are retained in x86-recreation-transaction.json and x86-native-gui-recreation.json.

limitations: The older detail-0 and coarse stage-120 logs cannot identify their exact suboperation retroactively; they remain retained. This replay establishes a concrete serial qualification failure and its correction.
The corrected successful runs do not count observed BUSY replies; successful teardown and revocation are asserted, not a particular retry count.
Required GitHub checks, canonical integration and remaining v0.4 roadmap acceptance are pending.
